chunks: I said: 'Has there not come to you the news of the Overwhelming (al-Ghashiya)?' He said: 'Al-Qa'im will overwhelm them with the sword.'
He said, I said: '(What about) "faces, that Day, humiliated"?' He said: 'Submissive, unable to resist.'
He said, I said: '(What about) "labouring"?' He said: 'They acted contrary to what God revealed.'
He said, I said: '(What about) "toiling/appointing"?' He said: 'They appointed other than the masters of authority (Wulat al-Amr).'
He said, I said: '(What about) "entering into a blazing fire"?' He said: 'They will enter the fire of war in this world during the era of al-Qa'im, and in the Hereafter the fire of Hell.'

key_terms.الْغَاشِيَةُ: Al-Ghashiya — Surah 88 of the Quran, 'The Overwhelming'; here reinterpreted to refer to al-Qa'im overwhelming his enemies
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: Al-Qa'im — the Rising One; a title for Imam al-Mahdi (may God hasten his reappearance), the twelfth Imam who will rise with the sword to establish justice
key_terms.نَاصِبَةٌ: Nasiba — In the Quranic context means 'toiling/laboring'; the Imam reinterprets it as 'appointing/installing (others)', a wordplay on the verb nasaba (to appoint/erect)
key_terms.وُلَاةِ الْأَمْرِ: Wulat al-Amr — Masters/Guardians of authority; in Shia theology, refers specifically to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt as the legitimate religious and political authorities

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq interpret Surah al-Ghashiya in relation to Imam al-Mahdi (al-Qa'im)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a Shia esoteric interpretation of Surah al-Ghashiya (88), reinterpreting its eschatological imagery in terms of al-Qa'im (Imam al-Mahdi). Each Quranic phrase describing the fate of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment is given a dual meaning: a worldly punishment during al-Qa'im's uprising (including military defeat and political subjugation) and a spiritual punishment in the Hereafter. The term 'nasiba' (toiling/appointing) is interpreted as appointing rulers other than the rightful Imams (Wulat al-Amr), reflecting the Shia theological emphasis on legitimate Imamate.

en.hubeali: H 14461 – Sahl, from Muhammad, from his father has narrated: Abu Abdullahasws having said when it was said to himasws “[88:1] Has not there come to you the news of the overwhelming calamity?”, heasws said: ‘They will be overwhelmed by the sword of the Rising One (Al-Qaimasws)’.
He said, ‘I said, (What about) “[88:2] Some faces, that Day, will be humiliated”?’ Heasws said: ‘They will be so humiliated that they will not be able to bear the exclusion’.
He said, ‘I asked. ‘(What about) “[88:3] Labouring”?’ Heasws said: ‘Labouring for other than what Allahazwj Revealed’.
I then asked, (What about) “[88:3] Appointing”?’ Heasws replied: ‘Having appointed other than the Masterasws of the Command (Wali Al-Amr)’.

He says then I asked, (What about) “[88:4] Entering into burning fire”?’ Heasws replied: ‘Entering into the fire of the war in the world during the era of the Rising One (Al-Qaimasws), and in the Hereafter the Fire of Hell’.
en.sarwar: 13. Sahl, from Muhammad, from his father has narrated: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) having said when it was said to him (a.s.) “[88:1] Has not there come to you the news of the overwhelming calamity?”, he (a.s.) said: ‘They will be overwhelmed by the sword of the Rising One (Al-Qaim (a.s.))’.
He said, ‘I said, (What about) “[88:2] Some faces, that Day, will be humiliated”?’ He (a.s.) said: ‘They will be so humiliated that they will not be able to bear the exclusion’.
He said, ‘I asked. ‘(What about) “[88:3] Labouring”?’ He (a.s.) said: ‘Labouring for other than what Allah (azwj) Revealed’.
I then asked, (What about) “[88:3] Appointing”?’ He (a.s.) replied: ‘Having appointed other than the Master (a.s.) of the Command (Wali Al-Amr)’.

He says then I asked, (What about) “[88:4] Entering into burning fire”?’ He (a.s.) replied: ‘Entering into the fire of the war in the world during the era of the Rising One (Al-Qaim (a.s.)), and in the Hereafter the Fire of Hell’.
